open_points.subject: Project, Room and ArtifactPointer lifecycles after restore
open_points.text: R0-89 says “every change after it is lost” and that “Registry's guarantees … hold within each store's history”, while M01 says “active is never returned to”, M03 says a room is “never removed”, and M05 says pointer terminal transitions are “final”.
open_points.question: Are those lifecycle guarantees final only within one store history, so restoring an older backup may make an archived project active again, restore an anonymised or deleted project, remove rooms added later, or restore an earlier pointer status?
options: All lifecycle guarantees are scoped to the current store history and the restored backup state prevails
Only audit numbering and migration closure are history-scoped; the other finality guarantees must survive restoration
open_points.default_guess: Treat every lifecycle guarantee as scoped to one store history and use exactly the state held by the restored backup.

open_points.subject: Customer lifecycle after restore
open_points.text: R0-89 says changes after the backup are lost, while M04 says erasure is “written once and final” and that a Customer record persists “forever”.
open_points.question: May restoration from a pre-erasure backup make an erased Customer live again, restore removed personal data, or undo restriction, lifting, ending or resumption marks?
options: Yes; Customer facts and final erasure are final only within one store history
No; Customer erasure and relationship or restriction changes must be preserved independently across restored histories
open_points.default_guess: Restore the Customer exactly as the backup holds it, making finality apply only within that store history.

open_points.subject: AgentSession access after restore
open_points.text: R0-89 says “every change after it is lost” is lost, while R0-46 says revocation blocks “every later operation” and R0-61 says an erased project “leaves the granted set of every agent session”.
open_points.question: Can restoring an older backup reinstate a revoked grant or active project, remove a later grant, or restore an earlier pending access request and access version?
options: Yes; AgentSession access is restored exactly from the backup and the guarantees apply only within that history
No; access changes, especially revocations and removals caused by erasure, survive store restoration through some separate fact
open_points.default_guess: Restore AgentSession access exactly from the backup, including any grants and active or pending state it held.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry identity and erasure across restored histories
open_points.text: R0-89 says a restored store “begins its own history from the backup” and M09 says it begins from “the backup's last number”, but M09 also says the sequence number is the entry's distinguishing identity and R0-66 says erased old entries are “gone”.
open_points.question: Are audit entries in the backup the same entities continued into the new history or new history-local entities, and may sequence numbers used after the backup in the lost history be reused by different entries after restoration?
options: Entries in the backup retain their identities; sequence numbers are unique only within a store history and numbers from the abandoned suffix may be reused
Every restored history needs a distinct history identity combined with the sequence number
Sequence numbers remain globally unreusable across restoration and must be preserved outside the restored store
open_points.default_guess: Treat the restored prefix as the same entries and scope sequence-number uniqueness to the current store history, allowing numbers from the lost suffix to be reused.

open_points.subject: Identity of restored domain records
open_points.text: R0-89 says the owner puts a backup “in its place” but also says “That store begins its own history from the backup”; it does not say whether records loaded from the backup continue the former entities or are new store-history-local entities carrying the same identifiers.
open_points.question: Does a restored Project, Customer, Room, ArtifactPointer or AgentSession retain the identity of the record represented in the backup, or does the new store history contain distinct entities that reuse those identifiers?
options: The restored records are continuations of the same domain entities, with their facts rolled back to the backup
They are distinct entities in a new store history, and identity is the combination of store history and recorded identifier
open_points.default_guess: Treat restored records as the same domain entities identified by their retained identifiers, with facts reverted to the backup state.
